item.title: Seahawks release veteran player after trade on Tuesday
item.description: The Seattle Seahawks made a major addition to their offensive line on Tuesday, acquiring eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts . The trade gives Seattle an experienced interior blocker as it looks to improve its offense during the second half of the season. However, bringing Nelson to Seattle has also forced the Seahawks to make a roster adjustment. With a new guard joining the offensive line, the team has decided to move on from one of its younger players, creating a fresh opportunity for the incoming veteran to strengthen the unit. MORE: Colts reportedly make stance on Jonathan Taylor clear after trade with Seahawks Seahawks waive Christian Haynes The Seattle Seahawks Christian Haynes. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-USA TODAY Sports The Seahawks waived guard Christian Haynes to make room for Nelson on their 53-man roster (h/t ESPN’s Adam Schefter). Seattle selected Haynes in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft, with the 81st overall pick, after his college career at UConn. After acquiring All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson, the Seahawks waived guard Christian Haynes to make room on their 53-man roster. — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 27, 2026 Haynes’ departure comes as Seattle looks to address its interior offensive line. The team had rotated Haynes and rookie Beau Stephens at right guard earlier in the season while Anthony Bradford was sidelined on injured reserve. The waiver process allows another NFL team to claim Haynes and take over his contract. If no team claims him, he can become a free agent and explore other opportunities. What Quenton Nelson brings to the Seahawks Nelson was selected sixth overall by the Colts in the 2018 NFL Draft and quickly established himself as one of the league’s leading offensive guards. He has earned eight Pro Bowl selections and three first-team All-Pro honors, making him a significant addition for Seattle. The Seahawks sent Indianapolis a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick in exchange for Nelson. The move also addresses an area Seattle has struggled with this season. The Seahawks ranked 21st in pass-block win rate and 27th in run-block win rate. Nelson’s experience in both phases could help improve the team’s interior blocking and provide better protection for quarterback Sam Darnold. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Brad Keselowski Set to Reveal More About His NASCAR Future This Weekend
item.description: Photo by: Stan Szeto Brad Keselowski is preparing to address one of the biggest questions surrounding the NASCAR Cup Series as he gets ready to discuss his future plans this weekend at Martinsville Speedway. The 2012 Cup Series champion announced Tuesday that he will hold a press conference Saturday morning, where he plans to answer several questions about what comes next in his racing career. The announcement comes after weeks of speculation following his upcoming departure from RFK Racing. Keselowski has made it clear that he is not ready to walk away from racing, leaving fans eager to learn where he could compete in 2027. Keselowski’s RFK Racing Departure Keselowski’s future became a major storyline in September when he and RFK Racing announced they would part ways following the 2026 season. He joined the organization in 2022 as both a driver and co-owner, helping transform the team into a more competitive operation. However, the two sides ultimately disagreed over his future role. RFK wanted him to transition toward a greater focus on competition management, while Keselowski wanted to continue driving. He also made an unsuccessful attempt to purchase the organization, adding another layer of uncertainty to his next move. Where Could Keselowski Go Next? Several possibilities have emerged as NASCAR teams prepare for the 2027 season. Keselowski could pursue another full-time Cup Series opportunity, although many seats have already been filled. A move into the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series has also been discussed. Keselowski has expressed interest in the possibility, which could give him another opportunity to compete for a championship while continuing his career. Another option could involve a combination of driving and leadership responsibilities with a different organization. Keselowski has experience in both areas, making him an attractive candidate for teams looking to improve their performance. However, he has not confirmed a new team or finalized his plans. NASCAR Fans Await Answers Saturday’s press conference could provide an important update, although Keselowski has only promised to address several questions rather than announce a definitive deal. At 42 years old, Keselowski remains a proven competitor with 36 Cup Series victories and a championship on his résumé. His next decision could have a major impact on the 2027 NASCAR season. For now, fans will have to wait until Martinsville to learn more about the future of one of the sport’s most accomplished drivers.

item.title: Historic Scottish golf course submerged by Storm Boelo flooding, faces extensive damage
item.description: A Scottish golf course has issued an update on its future after Storm Boelo submerged it over the weekend. Aerial photos taken Tuesday show the golf course almost completely underwater, and the club says the damage is "difficult to imagine right now." Founded in 1888, Dumbarton Golf Club is a historic 18-hole parkland course in the heart of the town, regarded as one of the oldest golf clubs in the west of Scotland. The club's management team said they wanted to provide an update after "the devastation from Saturday night" and thanked those who got in touch to offer help. They said: "We are monitoring the water coming in from the collapsed embankment as this will not be a quick fix. We have liaised with West Dunbartonshire Council, and their priority is, rightly, to close the towpath for safety reasons. They will then review the situation with engineers, but there is no guidance on timescales for this. "Therefore, we are left to try and do what we can to get the water off the course as quickly as possible. This will probably result in extra pumps being required at our cost. We are currently trying to secure these. "The damage to the course once the water has receded is difficult to imagine right now. "Bunkers may all need to be re-sanded, multiple bridges will need to be rebuilt, debris will take time to remove, and there are a number of damaged trees that we cannot get to. This will result in a significant cost as well." The management team went on to say they have decided to reduce the club’s operating hours to save money. They added: "This is heartbreaking, given that we have been doing so much in the clubhouse. We would ask members to support the club wherever possible and follow the revised opening hours, which will be sent out regularly. "We have received offers of help from various nearby golf courses. This has been extremely welcome, and we thank Helensburgh Golf Club, Cardross Golf Club and Clydebank and District Golf Club for reaching out to us at this time. "This is still very much an ongoing situation, and we will try to update you as we know more. Please bear with us as much as possible." The update came after we reported on Tuesday afternoon that the yellow warning for high winds covering the whole of Scotland and the far north-east of Northern Ireland has been cut short. Forecasters now predict the bad weather will end at 6 p.m., three hours earlier than expected. Storm-hit communities across Scotland are asking "serious questions" as politicians say "significant lessons" must be learned from the devastation left by Storm Boelo. Storm Boelo pummelled the north of the UK over the weekend, bringing 84mph gusts and a third of a month’s rain to pockets of Scotland. Richard Baines, curator of Logan Botanic Garden, was killed after being hit by a falling tree during the storm. The 60-year-old was pronounced dead at the scene at Mid Kelton near Castle Douglas around 10.30 a.m. on Sunday morning. This article originally appeared on Golfweek

item.title: Former Washington Nationals GM Mike Rizzo getting interviewed by the Astros
item.description: JUPITER, FL - FEBRUARY 13: President of Baseball Operations Mike Rizzo of the Washington Nationals talks to media during the 2025 Grapefruit League Spring Training Media Day at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium on Thursday, February 13, 2025 in Jupiter, Florida. (Photo by Jared Blais/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images When he was fired in July of 2025, I was curious to see what was next for Mike Rizzo. At the time, he was 64 years old, but he did not seem to have any desire to step away. After a year on the sidelines, Rizzo is in the mix for the Astros GM job. Yesterday, Bob Nightengale reported that Rizzo would get an interview. Houston Astros interviewing World Series architect Mike Rizzo for open GM job https://t.co/jghLc6RrTp — Bob Nightengale (@BNightengale) October 26, 2026 We will see if he gets the job, but I would sure be curious to see how he would do in Houston. The Nats and Astros also have quite a few connections. Obviously, Houston was the team that Mike Rizzo’s Nats beat in the 2019 World Series. The two clubs also share a Spring Training site at West Palm Beach. If Rizzo gets hired, we will be seeing a lot of him during Spring Training. It would be very interesting to contrast how the two teams do things at the same Spring Training site. Rizzo’s successor in DC, Paul Toboni, has changed a lot since he took over. The “I don’t care how hard you throw ball four” signs have been replaced by Traject Machines and other tech. Despite Rizzo being an old school guy, I do not think it would be impossible for him to have success in Houston. He would have to adapt some, but a veteran Astros team that is not afraid to spend money would suit Rizzo better than a young, smaller budget club. Rizzo may not be an innovator at this stage of his career, he still has an eye for a good trade and does a solid job with pro scouting. I still believe that he will have to lean into analytics more than he did, but maybe he has learned some lessons since being let go in DC. That is definitely something that will be brought up in his interview which is taking place today. Source: Mike Rizzo, the former Nationals GM, is in Houston interviewing for the GM job with the Astros, confirming @BNightengale report. — Brian McTaggart (@brianmctaggart) October 27, 2026 Based on his past achievements, Rizzo would be a strong candidate. He turned the Nats into one of the best teams in baseball last decade. However, the 2020’s have been a different story for Rizzo. Bad drafting and an inability to adapt led to him losing his edge. How much of this was his fault and how much was he hamstrung by the Lerner’s? If he gets the Astros job, we will be able to find out. He built a World Series championship team and won the NL East four times, but there is not a ton of recent success here. It is also no lock that Rizzo gets the job either. item.title: Liverpool Identify This Bundesliga Defender As A Top Target: Good Option For Iraola?
item.description: Liverpool Identify This Bundesliga Defender As A Top Target: Good Option For Iraola? Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast , journalist Pete O’Rourke claimed that Liverpool have identified Borussia Dortmund defender Nico Schlotterbeck as a target. O’Rourke said, “Nico Schlotterbeck is a long-term target, the Borussia Dortmund and Germany centre-back who was linked with the move to Liverpool last summer. He signed a new deal but I’m sure is a player who is still on their radar. “Then you’ve got the likes of Murillo at Forest, he is another player that Liverpool have looked at. I’m sure there’ll be other potential targets as well. “Bastoni at Inter Milan is a player that’s been a long-term target for the Reds, and then Jules Kounde as well at Barcelona, although he’s played right back primarily for them, he can also play at centre-back, and his future at Camp Nou is uncertain.” Schlotterbeck’s Impressive Form In The Bundesliga Schlotterbeck has enjoyed a good run of form for the German club in this campaign so far as he has put in a few solid performances for them on the defensive end of the field. The 26-year-old has registered one goal in six appearances for Borussia Dortmund this season on all fronts. The German talent is currently among the most talented centre-backs in the Bundesliga. Hence, it is no surprise that the Reds are showing interest in recruiting him next year. DORTMUND, GERMANY – OCTOBER 09: Nico Schlotterbeck of Borussia Dortmund runs with the ball during the Bundesliga 2026/27 match between Borussia Dortmund and SV Werder Bremen at Signal Iduna Park on October 09, 2026 in Dortmund, Germany. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images) His current contract at Signal Iduna Park will run out in the summer of 2031, which could make it tough for Liverpool to sign him on a cut-price deal this January or at the end of this campaign. Will Schlotterbeck Be A Good Option For Liverpool? Schlotterbeck is a good tackler of the ball and can time his challenges well to earn possession back for his team inside his half. He usually puts his foot through the ball when needed and is a tidy passer as well from the back. Standing at 1.91m, the German sensation is a strong presence in the air as well. However, there are some question marks on whether he can cope with the high intensity of the Premier League if the Reds manage to bring him on board next year. We can expect Schlotterbeck to add more quality and depth to Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola’s defence. He has what it takes to fight for a regular first-team spot at Anfield in the coming years. At 26, Schlotterbeck has his peak years ahead of him, which makes him a decent option for the Merseyside club to pursue in 2027. However, Iraola has to give him some time to adjust to life in England before he can get the best out of the player.

item.title: Incredible World Cup hero is coming to Liverpool
item.description: Incredible World Cup hero is coming to Liverpool An incredible wonderkid is coming to Liverpool who has become a World Cup hero for his country. The Julian Ward era has begun at Anfield. There's hope that it will be as fruitful as the promise shown by his predecessor, Richard Hughes. Liverpool have invested in their future over the last few years. The Reds have surrendered immediate success for a long-term vision buying future superstars in order to shed their veterans and build an exciting young squad. Hughes' strategy involved buying some of the best young players on the market. Florian Wirtz, Jeremy Jacquet, Hugo Ekitike, Milos Kerkez and Bradley Barcola all fall into that category. They have subsequently become the foundations for this current Liverpool team. Sprinkled in are some even younger players like Rio Ngumoha and Trey Nyoni. Meet Liverpool's stars of the future And there are even more youngsters hoping to become key players in the club's future. There are high hopes for Joshua Abe, who made a first-team appearance in pre-season. Ifeanyi Ndukwe currently out on loan and catching the eye at Levante is another exciting young centre-back. Alongside him Liverpool have Mor Talla Ndiaye playing some brilliant football for the U21 team. Will Wright simply cannot stop scoring and has been in magnificent form having already reached double figures for the U21 and U19 teams combined. There's Lucca Brughmanns who became the most expensive U23 goalkeeper of all time when he was signed by the Reds. And let's not forget about Luca Eden, who is producing special performances week in, week out at academy level and earning comparisons to Steven Gerrard. Another incredible wonderkid to add to Liverpool's list - Michael Mulholland Soon, Liverpool fans will become to know the name Michael Mulholland very well, too. Liverpool have agreed to sign the youngster when he celebrates his 16th birthday next year and he is expected to join the club in the January window. Until then, Mulholland is playing his club football in Northern Ireland for Crusaders FC, where he already scored his first goal for the senior team becoming the youngest to ever find the back of the net at that level in the club's history. Now, Mulholland is catching the eye at the U15 World Cup. He scored seven goals and registered one assist in his first four appearances at the tournament so far. He has guided his country to the round of 32 of the tournament and they will face Venezuela on Wednesday morning to see if they can get even further in the knock-out rounds. But already Mulholland is his country's World Cup hero, and soon he will on his way to Liverpool.

item.description: FILE PHOTO - Fenerbahçe head coach Ismail Kartal attends a press conference, ahead of Thursday's UEFA Europa Conference League round of 16 soccer match against Royale Union Saint Gilloise. (is associated with: «Fenerbahçe coach quits a month after previous resignation») Virginie Lefour/Belga/dpa Fenerbahçe coach Ismail Kartal has resigned less than 24 hours after the Istanbul derby defeat against Galatasaray. "After talks with our club leadership, this decision was accepted by mutual agreement and with mutual recognition and appreciation," Fenerbahçe said in a statement on Tuesday after the 2-1 league defeat. Fener are fifth, six points behind leaders Galatasaray. In September, Kartal also offered his resignation but Fenerbahçe president Aziz Yildirim rejected it. According to Yildirim, Kartal was then upset by a fan throwing a bottle at his head. His fourth spell as coach at Fener ends after only a few months. He had previously managed the club in 2014-2015, 2022 and 2023-2024. The derby between arch-rivals Galatasaray and Fenerbahçe on Monday was overshadowed by a fracas after the final whistle. item.title: Trey Nyoni On Liverpool Chances as Iraola Embraces Youth and Rotation
item.description: With Liverpool heading into the 2026-27 season without making any signings to address their depth issues in midfield, the chances were always high that 19-year-old academy graduate Trey Nyoni would be given chances to show what he could do by new head coach Andoni Iraola. It might even be fair to say Liverpool’s hopes for the season reseted in part on Nyoni being able to take those chances when they did come. To his credit, and rather fortunately for the team, he’s done just that. The youngster has made nine appearances to date, seeing the pitch in 75% of the games played in all competitions and earning 373 minutes—numbers which would project to 1,500-2,000 minutes across the entire season. “My motive has always just been,whet her I’m on the pitch for a minute, five minutes, 10 minutes, 90 minutes, I just try to make the most out of the minutes I get,” Nyoni said ahead of Wednesday’s League Cup tie against Chelsea, which he is widely expected to start. “But I think in the last few weeks obviously I’ve had a lot of exposure, which has been good for me. It’s something different, playing a lot of minutes within a short space of tim, but it has been really good.” He’s not the only youngster seeing big minutes early as Iraola looks to navigate a season where the Red will be trying to go deep and compete for silverware in four competitions despite a squad largely seen as thin at multiple positions and not just in midfield, with Rio Ngumoha and Lewis Koumas also seeing plenty of action. “For me it’s positive to see the younger players,” Nyoni added. “Obviously we need to stick together, help each other as much as possible. We know that being here, it’s not easy, there’s a lot of world-class players here. They’re going to push us every day. “I think having that allows us to keep pushing on and keep progressing. Every time we go on the pitch, I think none of us are really nervous—I think we all go out there and give 100%. That’s what’s important.”

item.title: Gronk Says 49ers Beat Themselves More Than Falcons Won
item.description: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports Rob Gronkowski believes the San Francisco 49ers lost to the Atlanta Falcons because they failed themselves, not because Atlanta played a perfect game. The former tight end pointed to a long history of injuries plaguing the 49ers roster before Sunday’s 29-20 loss at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. He argues that the team’s magic will return once healthy players like Mike Evans come back after the bye week. The 49ers dropped their first game of the season on Sunday, October 25. They now sit at 6-1 overall but face a critical injury list. According to Heavy.com , Gronkowski voiced serious worry regarding the injury bug still affecting the squad. He remains a firm believer that these issues will not affect the team in the long run. The Injury Cycle Question Gronkowski asked a blunt question during his podcast. “Why are the 49ers always injured? We’re not even talking about this year, not last year, I’m talking about the last 4-5 years. Why are they always injured?” He noted that many guys are on injured reserve but designated to return. The panic meter for the San Francisco 49ers is not going off according to him. On Monday, roughly 24 hours following the defeat, head coach Kyle Shanahan addressed the media. Shanahan disclosed that seven players stand a strong likelihood of returning after the bye week. Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Demarcus Robinson are among those included in that group. Nick Bosa, the star pass rusher, is expected to return after missing the last few weeks. Self-Inflicted Wounds The core of the loss was not a lack of talent from Atlanta. Gronkowski further stated that magic will diminish somewhat if weapons around you are absent. He thinks the magic will return immediately once Mike Evans and company resume play after the bye week. His final take on the game was sharp and direct. “The 49ers beat themselves more than the Atlanta Falcons won this game.” This statement cuts through the noise of the final score. Brock Purdy, who is currently playing at an MVP level, functions as a huddle extension of Kyle Shanahan per Gronk. The system works when the personnel is healthy. The Falcons just capitalized on the mistakes San Francisco made. Atlanta’s Path Forward The Falcons are now 4 spots higher in power rankings according to reports. They sit at No. 21 after the upset win. This team faces its true challenge on the defensive side. Jeff Ulbrich’s unit sits fourth against the run yet ranks only 29th against the pass. Converting high pressure numbers into sacks is the key to the next game. In Week 9, James Pearce will become eligible to return from suspension which will help the pass rush. The Falcons must keep Penix upright to beat them. The 49ers loss proves that even the best teams can fall if they hurt themselves first.

item.title: Scotland sweep aside Danes in European Championship opener
item.description: [Getty Images] Scotland women began their bid for European Curling Championship glory with a comprehensive 12-3 victory over Denmark. Fay Henderson's rink edged the opening two ends by single points before the Danes halved the deficit. However, the Scots took control of their opening match in Ostrava, surging into a five-point lead by the end of the fourth end. Although Denmark scored two points in the fifth, Scotland ended the contest emphatically with a six-point haul in the sixth and final end. Henderson's rink return to action on Thursday when they face Sweden, while Scotland men, led by Grant Hardie, begin their campaign against the Netherlands on Wednesday (07:30 GMT) - both matches are available to watch live on the BBC. item.title: Fleetwood-Arsenal halted for eight minutes because of drone
item.description: Referee Michael Salisbury spoke to both sides as play was halted [Getty Images] Arsenal's match with Fleetwood Town in the last-16 of the Carabao Cup was delayed for more than eight minutes after a drone was flown above the stadium during the match. Referee Michael Salisbury stopped play with one minute and 40 seconds on the clock after spotting the drone flying above the pitch while Arsenal waited to take a free-kick at Highbury Stadium. The game was halted while the referee spoke to the management and staff on both benches with police also investigating. The match got back underway with 10 minutes on the clock; the commentator on Sky saying police had located the drone operator. More to follow. item.title: LeBron James Is Showing His Value Early With the Philadelphia 76ers
item.description: Photo by: Bill Streicher LeBron James is already making an impact with the Philadelphia 76ers, even if his first few games have not been perfect. The 41 year old superstar joined Philadelphia during the offseason hoping to help the franchise compete for an NBA championship, and his early performances have shown that he can still contribute in multiple ways. Through three regular season appearances, James is averaging 16.3 points, seven rebounds and 5.7 assists per game. Philadelphia won his first two games before suffering a 106-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Sunday. Although the season is still young, James has given the 76ers reasons to be encouraged about what he can bring to their revamped roster. LeBron Is Doing More Than Scoring James has not needed to dominate the ball to make an impact. His passing, rebounding and basketball IQ have helped Philadelphia organize its offense while building chemistry with his new teammates. In his Philadelphia debut against the New York Knicks, James recorded 14 points, nine rebounds and seven assists in a 106-100 victory. He followed that performance with 17 points, 10 rebounds and five assists against the Cleveland Cavaliers as the 76ers rallied from a 29 point deficit to win 114-106. Those performances demonstrated how James can influence a game without having to carry the scoring load every night. With Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown providing additional offensive firepower, Philadelphia has several players capable of creating their own shots. James can focus on making the right reads, finding open teammates and taking advantage of defensive mismatches. An Unexpected Challenge at Center James also found himself in an unusual position against Detroit. With Joel Embiid and several other frontcourt players unavailable, Philadelphia started James at center. He finished with 18 points and five assists, but the 76ers struggled defensively and lost their first game of the season. James has made it clear that playing center is not something he expects to do regularly. With Embiid serving as Philadelphia’s primary big man, the team needs its frontcourt depth to get healthier. The experience nevertheless showed James’ willingness to take on different responsibilities when his team needs him. Can LeBron Help Philadelphia Win a Championship? Philadelphia has assembled a talented roster, and James’ championship experience could become one of its biggest advantages. His leadership and ability to control the pace of a game should help the 76ers as they work to develop chemistry. There are still concerns about his shooting efficiency, workload and the team’s rebounding. James also missed the victory over Milwaukee while managing a back issue, making workload management important early in the season. Still, his first few appearances have offered encouraging signs. item.title: Wildcat Wrap: Arizona men’s golf tested against top competition at East Lake Cup
item.description: Editor’s note: With several sports going on, Wildcat Wrap serves as a recap that focuses on the Arizona programs that we do not have the time to cover on a regular basis but are certainly worthy of recognition. Fresh off one of the best postseason runs in program history, the Arizona men’s golf program is getting a test of where it stands against top-ranked teams at this week’s East Lake Cup in Atlanta, Georgia. Arizona finished fourth of out of four teams in the stroke play portion of the tournament. The Wildcats shot one-over par, behind Auburn (13-under), Oklahoma State (11-under) and UCLA (8-under). The four programs were the semifinalists in last year’s NCAA Championships. Arizona fell to UCLA in the national semifinal match. Auburn went on to beat UCLA for the national title. Tianyi Xiong led Arizona Monday in stroke play with a 2-under to finish sixth individually. On Tuesday, Arizona fell to Auburn in match play by a score of 4-1. The lone point came from Xiong. Auburn is the No. 3 team in the nation. Arizona entered the tournament unranked. In addition to Xiong, Arizona’s starting lineup incudes returners William Wistrand and Matej Baca . Arizona has two newcomers in its lineup: UTRGV transfer Jorge Sampedro and freshman Adam Fahey . Swimming and diving Swimming and diving earned a split against SMU in a home meet over the weekend. The Wildcats women won 211-89 while the men lost 155-144. Kelsey Wasikowski led the women with a pair of individual wins in the 100 yard breast and 200 yard breast. She was also part of a first-place relay in the 200 yard medley relay. Tomas Lukminas guided the men with wins in the 50 yard free and 100 yard free. He was part of the 400 yard free relay that took first place. Arizona next competes in a four-team meet in Los Angeles on Nov. 7 between former Pac-12 rivals UCLA, USC and ASU. Women’s golf The women’s golf team competed at the Abilene Christian Intercollegiate last week, finishing in a tie for fifth in a crowded field. Arizona shot 5-over par across three rounds. Champion Oregon led the field with a 28-under. Sophomore Kinsley Ni finished second overall with a score of 9-under. Ni was the only Wildcats golfer to shoot under par. Arizona has the rest of the year off before returning in February for the Thunderbird Intercollegiate, which will be held at Tucson Country Club.

item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 30: Cam York #8 of the Philadelphia Flyers skates during a game against the Pittsburgh Penguins at Xfinity Mobile Arena on September 30, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images) Getty The Philadelphia Flyers executed a few key roster moves ahead tonight’s matchup against the Columbus Blue Jackets, headlined by defensemen Cam York from injured reserve and the recall of forward Jacob Gaucher. Transactions: Forward Jacob Gaucher has been recalled from the @LVPhantoms (AHL). Additionally, defenseman Cam York has been activated off injured reserve. Defenseman Rasmus Ristolainen has been placed on injured reserve (upper-body injury) retroactive to Oct. 24. — Philadelphia Flyers (@NHLFlyers) October 27, 2026 Cam York Returns to Stabilize the Blue Line After missing eight games with an upper-body injury, top-four defensemen Cam York has officially been activated off injury reserve. The 25-year-old blueliner, who averaged over 21 minutes of ice time per game prior to his injury, is expected to return immediately to provide a much needed boost to Philadelphia’s defense. During York’s absence, the team suffered a 3-4-1 record. The Flyers placed veteran defensemen Rasmus Ristolainen on injured reserve Monday, clearing a spot for York on the roster. Ristolainen suffered an upper-body injury and is expected to be out for roughly two weeks. Jacob Gaucher Back Up with the Flyers The Flyers officially recalled center Jacob Gaucher from their AHL affiliate, the Lehigh Valley Phantoms on Tuesday. Gaucher was reassigned to the Phantoms on Sunday, marking a quick turnaround back to the NHL. The 25-year-old forward gives head coach Rick Tocchet flexibility down the middle as the team struggles to stay out of the Metropolitan Division basement. The Flyers head into tonight’s matchup with a record of 3-7-3, marking them seventh in the Metropolitan Division. With York back on the ice and Gaucher back on the roster, the Flyers look to string together momentum as they face division rivals in back-to-back games, starting with Columbus at the Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia tonight at 7 p.m. EST. item.description: Fleetwood Town ’s blockbuster match with Arsenal in the Carabao Cup was delayed by around eight minutes due to the presence of an unauthorised drone hovering over the pitch. The momentous match for the League Two minnows at Highbury had only just kicked off when the players spotted the drone flying in the sky above the stadium. Eventually, referee Salisbury took the decision to call all 22 players off the pitch in the eighth minute, although the drone then appeared to fly away fro the pitch. Play resumed once the drone had been dealt with (Getty) There was confusion as the referee stopped play to speak to both managers (PA) The police were also called, while there was confusion and anger in the stands, before it was reported that the operator of the drone had been identified and dealt with. item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 25: Seattle Seahawks general manager John Schneider looks on prior to a game against the Los Angeles Rams in the NFC Championship game at Lumen Field on January 25, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) Getty The Seattle Seahawks have made their blockbuster trade with the Indianapolis Colts. It just wasn’t the one many fans expected. Seattle agreed to acquire eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson on Tuesday, Oct. 27, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. The Seahawks are sending a 2027 third-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection to Indianapolis in exchange for the veteran offensive lineman. The acquisition provides a significant upgrade to Seattle’s offensive line, but it also raises questions about the team’s reported pursuit of Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. Seattle was among four teams connected to Taylor in a report published Sunday. Now, general manager John Schneider has spent another premium draft pick to address a different position, while two of the Seahawks’ existing running backs are approaching potential returns from injuries. Seattle’s decision to acquire Nelson doesn’t eliminate the possibility of another deal, but it changes the equation. According to Schefter, the Seahawks are sending their 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection to Indianapolis for Nelson. That further reduces a collection of future draft picks Schneider had already tapped into. Seattle previously traded its 2027 fourth-round selection to the Cleveland Browns during the 2026 NFL draft to acquire the pick used on offensive lineman Beau Stephens. item.title: Should the Eagles Turn to Joe Milton After Another Disappointing Loss?
item.description: Photo by: Jerome Miron Joe Milton could be the next quarterback to get an opportunity with the Philadelphia Eagles as the team searches for answers during a difficult stretch of the 2026 NFL season. Philadelphia suffered another disappointing loss Monday night, falling 38-21 to the Dallas Cowboys. Tanner McKee started in place of the injured Jalen Hurts, but the Eagles could not maintain their momentum after briefly taking the lead in the third quarter. With the team dropping five consecutive games, questions are beginning to emerge about whether Philadelphia should give Milton a chance to lead the offense. McKee Has Not Done Enough to Silence Questions McKee entered the starting role with an opportunity to prove he could keep the Eagles competitive while Hurts recovers. However, Philadelphia has struggled to find consistency on offense, and Monday’s loss added to the frustration. McKee finished with 211 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception against Dallas. Although he showed some positive moments, the Eagles ultimately struggled to keep pace with the Cowboys in the second half. The difficult circumstances surrounding McKee should not be ignored. He has limited starting experience and was not originally expected to carry the offense for an extended period. Still, Philadelphia needs better results if it hopes to turn its season around. What Joe Milton Could Bring Milton offers something different. The former Tennessee Volunteers quarterback possesses tremendous arm strength and athletic ability, giving the Eagles a potential option to stretch the field and create plays outside the pocket. Philadelphia signed Milton off the Cowboys’ practice squad after Hurts was sidelined. While Milton has appeared in NFL games, he remains relatively inexperienced and has yet to establish himself as a reliable starter. His physical tools could make him an intriguing option, especially if the Eagles believe the offense needs a different approach. However, arm strength alone does not guarantee success. Milton would need to demonstrate that he can make smart decisions, protect the football and operate the offense consistently. Should Philadelphia Make the Change? The Eagles should seriously consider giving Milton an opportunity if McKee continues to struggle. With the team searching for answers, evaluating another quarterback could provide valuable information about its options moving forward. However, Milton should not automatically receive the starting job simply because he has more exciting physical tools. Philadelphia should evaluate both quarterbacks in practice and determine who gives the offense the best chance to succeed. If McKee cannot deliver improved results, turning to Milton could be a worthwhile gamble. The Eagles need a spark, and Milton may be worth a look.

The offense was really struggling to get anything going early this season, and Payton felt a change was needed. Well, the Broncos made the switch in Week 5, and they're 3-0 since then. But that doesn't tell the full story. As ESPN's Jeff Legwold highlighted, the Broncos offense has actually regressed in one very important phase of the game: third downs. Payton's version of this offense is worse on third downs than Webb's, as they're struggling to convert all kinds of third downs. Broncos' third-down production has gotten worse since Sean Payton took over "Since coach Sean Payton took back playcalling duties in Week 5, the offense has gotten worse on third down," Legwold writes. "Denver was 4-26 (15.4%) on third down in the two games combined before Sunday." Payton's first two games didn't go well on third down, and even in their Week 7 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals , the Broncos went just 3-of-11 on third down. Denver went 2-of-12 in Week 1, 4-of-11 in Week 2, 7-of-13 in Week 3, and 8-of-17 in Week 4 on third downs with Webb as the play-caller. Overall, the Denver offense went 21-of-53 on third down with Webb calling the plays in Weeks 1 through 4 (39.6%), and in three games with Payton as the play-caller, the Broncos offense has gone 7-of-37 (18.9%) on third down. MORE : Browns not expected to trade Jerry Jeudy despite plenty of speculation The Broncos have clearly regressed since Payton took over, with their third-down conversions with Payton being more than twice as worse as it was under Webb. That's made worse by the context that Webb's version of the offense faced the Kansas City Chiefs , Jacksonville Jaguars , Los Angeles Rams , and San Francisco 49ers , while Payton's faced the Los Angeles Chargers , Seattle Seahawks , and Cardinals. While the Seahawks are the most challenging defense on that schedule, the Cardinals and Chargers are two of the worst defenses in the NFL. For Payton's offense to struggle that much on third down against them is a bad sign. While the Broncos' win-loss record looks better with Payton calling the plays again, this important third-down statistic shows the offense has taken a noteworthy step back since he took over play-calling duties in Week 5.
